title: Percentage error
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:39Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches percentage error (the error as a percentage of the true value); the closest, the accuracy-of-measurements point, covers only absolute error and limits of accuracy, which is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Percentage error
card: Error = estimate − true value. Ignore the sign to find the size of the error: it is the gap between the two.
Percentage error = error ÷ true value × 100%. Always divide by the true value, not by the estimate.
A small percentage error means the estimate is close to the true value. The same error matters more when the true value is small.
Example: you estimate 45 people, and the true number is 50. The error is 5, so 5 ÷ 50 × 100% = 10%.
draft.remember: Divide the size of the error by the true value, then multiply by 100.

a.q: Sam measures a board as 2.4 m. Its true length is 2.5 m. What is the percentage error?
a.why: The error is 0.1 m. Then 0.1 ÷ 2.5 × 100% = 4%. The answer 4.17% divides by the estimate 2.4 instead of the true value.
a.clue: Which number goes on the bottom of the fraction?

b.q: A crowd is estimated at 1200. The true count is 1000. What is the percentage error?
b.why: The error is 1200 − 1000 = 200. Then 200 ÷ 1000 × 100% = 20%. The answer 16.7% divides by the estimate 1200 instead of the true value.
b.clue: The true value is the number that was actually counted.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers are correct: 0.1 ÷ 2.5 × 100% = 4% and 200 ÷ 1000 × 100% = 20%, and the distractors reflect real mistakes such as dividing by the estimate.
